history.provenance:
Beverley, Yorkshire, Minster (collegiate church) of St John the Evangelist
This attribution was accepted (albeit with a query) in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964). However, the attribution was later rejected in the Supplement (1987). The corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card recorded the following information, which was later was deemed unsatisfactory for an attribution (and crossed through):Consists of part of a s. xii mass-book with the kalendar, temporale (in part), and canon of the mass; part of a s. xiii mass-book not of York use, but corrected and partly adapted for it, containing a further portion of the temporale; and a s. xv addition with the rest of the temporale, masses for the dedication of a church and part of the sanctorale, all of York use. Traditionally said to have belonged first to Beverley and then to Roche abbey. Information from English Church History Exhibition (St Albans, 1905), p. 9 - loan from Bishop of Truro (John Gott). Compare W. H. Frere in York Minster Historical Tracts: The earliest MS. [missal] has passed from the library of Dr Gott and has not been traced. See also York Manual, Surtees Society 59 (1874), i. vii-x; W. H. Frere Bibliotheca musico-liturgica, no. 659.

provenance.p: This attribution was accepted (albeit with a query) in the second edition of Medieval Libraries of Great Britain (1964). However, the attribution was later rejected in the Supplement (1987). The corresponding Medieval Libraries of Great Britain index card served only to redirect the reader to the entry for Beverley.

history.provenance: Dr John Gott, bishop of Truro (1830–1906). Library sold: Sotheran, Bibliotheca Pretiosa 1907 and Sotheby, 26 February and 20 March 1908, 21 July 1910.
